experiment: Realistic (non-oracle) RAG baseline vs the oracle RAG upper bound (reviewer request)
retriever: Live entity resolution: molecular names -> PubChem (formula+SMILES); crystalline/formation-energy -> name->formula->Materials Project most-stable polymorph (space group / formation energy). No GT peeking; retrieval genuinely misses or returns the wrong polymorph. Facts prepended to the prompt, single generation, no loop (same path as oracle rag_in_prompt).

molecular.note: every compound is name-addressable in PubChem, so realistic ~= oracle

crystalline.note: composition-keyed MP misses mineral names; when it resolves it returns the MOST-STABLE polymorph, not the named phase (rutile #141 vs named #136, barium titanate #38 vs #99, pyrite #58 vs #205)

formation_energy.note: same composition-key miss; when resolved the stable-polymorph Ef matches within tol

finding: The oracle RAG is an upper bound. A realistic retriever matches it on molecular formula (err|commit 0.2% vs oracle 0.3%, baseline 21.7%) with low abstention (4.8%), because PubChem is name-addressable. On the long-tail crystalline and formation-energy surfaces it recovers almost none of the oracle gain: err|commit stays at baseline (EF 33.9% vs 31.3%; SG 5.3% vs 5.8%) while abstention rises to 56-59%, because composition-keyed MP retrieval covers only ~21-23% of entities and returns the most-stable polymorph rather than the named phase. Imperfect retrieval degrades exactly where the named entity needs phase disambiguation, the regime where Mode A's claim-specific retrieval still works.
metric_note: Reported as error-given-commitment (err|commit, abstention-invariant) with abstention alongside, using the paper-facing baseline (baseline_v3_final.json, EF 31.3%). Earlier draft labeled an abstention-excluded wrong-rate as 'ITT'; corrected. Under the paper's ITT definition (wrong+abstain) oracle molecular is ~42%, consistent with the existing 43% headline.
